page.h1: HTS Chapter 22: Beverages, Spirits and Vinegar — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Bourbon, Ethanol, Wine & Beverage Exports (HTS Ch. 22) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $10.80B of beverages in 2025: $4.91B of ethanol, $1.25B of whiskey incl. bourbon, $850M of wine. Who buys them and what each top buyer charges.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$10.80 billion** of Chapter 22 goods in 2025, down **1%** from 2024. Ethanol is the biggest part: heading 2207 (fuel and industrial ethanol) was **$4.91 billion**, 46% of the chapter, up 11%. Spirits followed at $2.74 billion, led by whiskey including bourbon (**$1.25 billion**, down 18%), then soft drinks and energy drinks ($1.70 billion), wine ($850 million, down 32%) and beer ($305 million). Canada is the largest buyer (**28%**), mostly ethanol and soft drinks, followed by the Netherlands (13%) and the UK (7%). Exports from January to August 2026 were 13% above the same months of 2025.

Tariffs are low for most of this trade: Canada and Mexico charge nothing on qualifying U.S. goods under USMCA, the EU, the UK and Japan let bourbon and other whiskey in duty-free, and the UK takes U.S. ethanol duty-free within a 1.4 billion-liter quota. What hit U.S. alcohol hardest was not a tariff but Canada’s provincial liquor boards, most of which stopped buying U.S. beer, wine and spirits in March 2025. The costly markets are India (100% on bourbon, 150% on other spirits and wine) and China, which stacks 2018 counter-tariffs and an extra 10% on its normal rate.

keyTakeaways: Ethanol, not bourbon, is the biggest U.S. Chapter 22 export: $4.91 billion in 2025, sold mostly to Canada, the Netherlands, India, the UK and Colombia.

Canada charges no tariff on U.S. drinks, but most provinces have kept U.S. beer, wine and spirits off government liquor-store shelves since March 2025, and Saskatchewan added a 50% levy on U.S. alcohol from September 8, 2026.
The EU and UK charge nothing on bourbon; the EU’s 2025 plan to put 30% on U.S. whiskey and wine is suspended with no end date, and the UK’s duty-free quota for U.S. ethanol renews on January 1, 2027.
India and China are where tariffs bite: bourbon pays 100% in India and about 40% in China without an exclusion, and China’s exclusions end on December 31, 2026.
